The Silicon Valley Archives:A Collections Explorer

The Silicon Valley Archives is a specific collecting project at Stanford University Libraries. But many collections, built over decades by curators across the Libraries, may be relevant to the study of the region and industries that we now know as Silicon Valley. This bibliography, based on recent scholarly approaches to the region summarized here, offers a lens on the many kinds of materials, and the wide variety of collections, that may be of interest to scholars working on the history of this place.

Much of the survey, selection, ranking, and placement work for this project was conducted by an LLM, with limited curatorial guidance. To avoid untrustworthy text, every title, date span, and description is required to come directly from the catalog or from finding aids. Collections the catalog does not describe are listed by title alone. Mistakes may nonetheless be possible: researchers should confirm any material in this document by checking the original catalog entries and/or finding aids.

Collections are placed by what they are about rather than by when they were made, so an oral history recorded in 1980 about the 1950s is filed under the 1950s. A collection that documents more than one period may appear under multiple periods. Within a period a collection is listed under one subject only; those that could not be placed under a specific heading have been placed at a general level. The result loses some opportunities for cross-reference but minimizes repetition. Researchers are encouraged to make use of subject headings in the catalog to explore further connections among these materials.

A ranking on a ten-point scale was produced by having an LLM evaluate catalog records and finding aids against a fixed set of curatorial criteria. Ranks one and two were excluded as not sufficiently relevant. Ranks three and above are provided, along with a user interface slider that allows for dynamic selection. Importantly, ranks do not reflect material quality and will not correspond with the interests of all scholars or communities—they reflect only one view of what may be most relevant to the study of Silicon Valley. A JSON file is provided so users may download much of the bibliographic material on which this site is based and produce ranking systems better suited to individual priorities.

Charles Petersen

Ohlone Period, ~ to 18th century#2 collections
  • The history of the region now known as Silicon Valley begins with the lives of the Ohlone People, who have resided, and continue to reside, along the Peninsula, the South Bay, and the wider San Francisco Bay Region since time immemorial. As with histories such as Fred Glass’s From Mission to Microchip (2016) and David Pellow and Lisa Park’s The Silicon Valley of Dreams (2002), we invite scholars conducting research on the long history of Silicon Valley to consider materials collected by our colleagues in allied fields such as the University Archaeology Collections as well as records drawn from projects of the Stanford Historical Society such as the Native American Alumni Oral Histories.

  • Jacquard loom patterns and samples, 1821 M3147 [3]#
    under a linear foot
    A unique book of patterns and descriptions created by an early user of the revolutionary Jaquard loom, identified as "Richaud" on the cover of the book. Illustrated with hand-drawn Jacquard loom patterns and fabric samples.
  • Visite de Msr le Duc d'Aumale a la Croix-Rousse, dans l'atelier de M. Carquillat : le 24 Août 1841 MISC 2898 MF [6]#
    1844
    Picture shows the Duc d'Aumale full length and facing right, accompanied by four members of his entourage; to his right, Carquillat, also full length but facing slightly left, holds his well-known portrait of Joseph Marie Jacquard; another full length male figure stands to the right of Carquillat, gesturing at the portrait. The figures are standing in Carquillat's workshop in front of the loom which produced both the portrait of Jacquard and the item here described; a workman stands at the loom, body pointed away but looking over his shoulder at D'Aurnale and Carquillat.

Memoirs and family papers#1
  • Harwood family papers, 1722-1962 M0206 [4*]#
    2 linear feet
    Over his lifetime, Andrew Allen Harwood (1802-1884), great grandson of Benjamin Franklin, kept letters and notes of interest and autographs in a collection known as ODDS & ENDS. Letters, notes, autographs, portraits, and other materials collected by the Harwood Family over a period of two hundred-fifty years. Much of the early materials, including Revolutionary War era materials, are navy and military service related.

    Thirty-six letters from Father Durán, in his role as administrator of Mission San Jose, to the fathers who held the office of Procurador of the Missions of California, concerning standing orders for supplies to the mission, and related financial and administrative matters.
  • Mission Santa Clara padrón, 1839 December 31 Vault B-101 [6]#

  • Cabinet noir coding and decoding tables, circa 1777-circa 1800 MISC 2037 MF [3]#

Labor and professional organizations#2
  • Chinese Railroad Workers [3]#
    1864 - 1866
    The Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project seeks to give a voice to the Chinese migrants whose labor on the Transcontinental Railroad helped to shape the physical and social landscape of the American West. The Chinese Railroad Workers Digital Materials Repository offers open access to materials that are selected for their qualities that they are difficult to retrieve, and rich for historical study.
  • Journal of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet, 1855-1856 MSS CODEX 1591 [4]#
    Journal kept by ship's carpenter William F. Harden documenting the second voyage of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet under Captain Andrews, departing New York for San Francisco, Hawaii, and Canton on August 18, 1855. The journal records Chinese longshoremen strikes, confiscation of liquor, brutal punishments including floggings, the death of the Captain's youngest son, the death of the ship's cook after repeated beatings, forced prizefights between ship's boys for crew entertainment, and other harsh conditions aboard ship.

Trade, merchandising and retail#5
  • Alfred Robinson papers, 1837-1859 MS Vault 049B [5]#
    under a linear foot
    Originally from Mass., Robinson first went to Calif. in 1829 as the representative for the hide-trading and shipping firm Bryant, Sturgis & Co. Primarily business correspondence to and from Robinson, in his role as a San Francisco merchant and as agent for the firm Howland & Aspinwall of New York, including: a letter book (Dec. 1848-June 1849) concerning prices of goods in San Francisco and suggesting cargoes to be sent to Calif. from the East coast; letters from Howland & Aspinwall in New York (1848-1849); and other business correspondence from various individuals and companies (1848-1849).
  • Jacob P. Leese papers MS 0010.OV [5]#
    2 linear feet; 1837-1862
    Consists of personal and business correspondence, indentures, legal documents, ship's papers, accounts, inventories, and maps, documenting the activities, business interests, and land holdings of early California merchant Jacob P. Leese, his wife Rosalia Vallejo de Leese, and his partner Thomas O. Larkin, between the years 1837 to 1862.
  • Letter from C. Curry Guns and Fancy Goods to Hardy & Kennedy regarding pistol order and firearms inventory, 1860 September 27. MISC 2954 [3]#

  • William A. Leidesdorff collection, 1834-1857, 1928 MS 1277 [4]#
    under a linear foot
    A prominent merchant and landowner, Leidesdorff also served in a number of civic positions, including United States vice-consul to Mexico (appointed by Thomas Larkin in 1845) and treasurer of San Francisco. Leidesdorff's business correspondence and records document his transactions with many prominent early Californians, including Yerba Buena alcaldes Francisco Guerrero and George Hyde; Thomas Larkin; William Davis Merry Howard; Samuel Brannan; Stephen Smith; Nathan Spear; Henry Dalton; Concepcion Avila; and Henry Mellus.
  • William D.M. Howard papers, 1823-1878 MS Vault 030 [3]#
    3 linear feet
    Howard was a merchant and financier in San Francisco, California. Correspondence, invoices, and receipts from pioneer Calif. residents, merchants, and companies, reflecting Howard's extensive commercial activities through his firm, Mellus & Howard Company, including letters to and from business partner Henry D. Mellus, Francis Mellus at the Los Angeles branch of the firm, Abel Stearns, Henry F. Teschemacher, and Joseph P. Thompson.

  • Carleton E. Watkins photograph collection PC RM Watkins [8]#

  • Chester Smith Lyman journals, 1845-1854 MS Vault 042 [3]#

  • Culver family papers, 1858-1915 M0633 [6]#
    8 linear feet
    Includes correspondence, diaries, and photographs. The Collection reflects J. O. Culver's experience as a lawyer, his service as an Army Paymaster and Post Office Inspector, his endeavors in small fruit culture, and his excursions into prospecting and mining. In general, the family letters and papers give a panorama of middle class society in New York, Wisconsin and Missouri, and Colorado and California, from 1860 to 1915, a familiar pattern in the United States of looking ever westward for opportunity.
  • Daingerfield family letters, 1850-1853 M0004 [3]#

  • Faxon Dean Atherton Papers MS Vault 005 [8]#
    4 linear feet; 1831-1932
    A native of Dedham, Massachusetts, Atherton first came to the Pacific coast around 1834 to work for a ship chandlery firm in Valparaiso, Chile. He settled in Valparaiso in 1840 and became a successful merchant dealing in hides and tallow, foodstuffs, and other commodities. The collection comprises business records and correspondence documenting Atherton's mercantile relationships and activities in Boston, California, Hawaii, and Valparaiso; correspondence, deeds, and other documents relating to Atherton's real estate investments in California, including Las Milpitas Ranch and Bolsa de San Cayetano Ranch in Monterey County, San Lorenzo Ranch in Alameda County, Los Putos Ranch in Solano County, and Valparaiso Park in San Mateo County; and legal documents and other papers concerning Atherton's estate after his death.

    5 linear feet
    Formerly a student of art, Andrew Putnam Hill became a professional photographer in 1889, opening a studio in San Jose, California with his partner, Sydney J. Yard. The images in this album primarily document the Palo Alto residence of Jane and Leland Stanford, the Palo Alto Stock Farm horses, and Stanford University.
  • Andrew Putnam Hill Photograph collection, 1890-1895 [8]#
    2 linear feet; 1890 - 1895
    Mounted albumen prints, commercially produced by Hill and his two studios, Hill & Yard and Hill & Watkins, of the newly established Stanford University and of the activity of the Palo Alto Stock Farm, upon which the University had been built.
  • Andrew Putnam Hill photographs PC0004 [7]#
    2 linear feet; 1853-1922
    This collection consists of mounted albumen prints commercially produced by A. P. Hill and his two studios, Hill and Yard and Hill and Watkins. Subjects include views of the Stanford University campus, interior and exterior shots of major buildings, events such as the university's opening day and the funeral of Leland Stanford, student groups, and the Palo Alto Stock Farm and horses.
  • Archibald J. Treat papers, 1883-1961 (inclusive), 1883-1941 (bulk) SC0511 [4*]#
    under a linear foot
    During the construction of Stanford University, Treat took photographs of the work in progress that were regularly sent to Leland Stanford to keep him informed. These papers pertain largely to Treat's association with Leland Stanford and the history of the University and include correspondence, a notebook (largely in shorthand), his typescript reminiscences, and two letters by his daughter pertaining to her father.
  • David Starr Jordan Papers [7]#
    Jordan was a naturalist-first a botanist and secondly and of greater significance an ichthyologist. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's voluminous correspondence (62.25 linear ft.) relating to professional and university matters, but also contains other types of material such as writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. He developed the idea of a junior college and was responsible for developing Stanford University into an intellectually competitive university rather than the technical training school envisioned by the founders.
  • David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981 SC0058 [8]#
    266 linear feet
    In the Spring of 1891, Leland Stanford offered Jordan the presidency of the university established in memory of the late son of Leland Stanford and Jane Lathrop Stanford. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's correspondence relating to professional and university matters, and also contains writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. Materials in the collection reflect Jordan's embrace of and advocacy for eugenics, including his leadership in 19th and 20th century eugenics organizations.
  • George Mann Richardson letter to Firstall SCM0149 [3]#
    under a linear foot; 1892 Apr 17
    Professor of Organic Chemistry at Stanford University (1891-1902). Letter recounting the first year at Stanford University, in particular difficulties from the lack of equipment, the success of the football team in its first game against Berkeley, and a hiking trip Richardson and his wife took from Stanford to Pescadero.
  • George T. Clark papers, 1862-1935 SC0292 [4*]#
    2 linear feet
    Clark was Stanford University Librarian, 1907-1928 (emeritus 1928 until his death in 1940) and co-founder and first president of the California Library Association. These papers relate primarily to Clark's research on the life of Leland Stanford and include correspondence, 1924-1935, historical documents, 1862-1893, clippings, photographs, and two notebooks, 1928-1930,for his comprehensive biography of Senator Leland Stanford, published by the Stanford University Press in 1931.
  • Grant founding and endowing the Leland Stanford Junior University SC1445 [9]#

  • Henry Z. Osborne papers SCM0173 [4*]#
    under a linear foot; 1892-1921

These papers consist of a letter from Leland Stanford (on U.S. Senate letterhead), 1892; a telegram from Jane L. Stanford, March 1896, thanking Osborne for his loyalty to Leland Stanford; a letter from David Starr Jordan about the Dept. of Mining at Stanford, 1899, with a mention of the success of Herbert C. Hoover (an early graduate of the Dept.); and a letter from John C. Branner, 1921, commenting on an article by Osborne and his opinion on Japan.

Represented in the collection are a variety of business papers including those documenting liquidation of Donohoe, Ralston and Company (1863-1867) when W. C.   • Frank Y. Chuck papers, 1912-2020 SC1550 [6]#
    5 linear feet

Chuck (1900-1994) was a research chemist who patented a technique for the dehydration of milk and the stabilization of whey products through crystallization so they would dissolve easily in liquid, a process that allowed milk products to be shipped overseas during wartime and is still used today in the production of household items such as instant hot cocoa mix and powdered milk.   • Boulder Dam (aka Hoover Dam) : film of construction, ca. 1936 M1057 [6]#
    Titled "The Construction of the Boulder Dam, 1931-1936," this film was sponsored by the Six Companies, edited by Dowling & Brownell, Hollywood. The film is in black & white and has intertitles and no soundtrack.
  • Charles David Marx papers, 1873-1942 SC0161 [8]#
    14 linear feet
    He came to Stanford in 1891 as Professor of Civil Engineering and taught here until his retirement in 1923. Correspondence, reports, research notes, manuscripts, drawings, financial records, clippings, minutes, reprints, and photographs largely pertaining to engineering projects, most of which concern dams and water systems in California; other subjects include his years as student and lecturer at Cornell University, his civic work, and other professional activities.
  • Electrolysis Survey on Treasure Island, 1939 June 16. MISC 1918 [4]#
    Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation." Describes Treasure Island's soil, the various systems on the island (such as water, gas, and sanitary), and describes the results of "tests made to determine the amount of electrical protection necessary to stop [...] leaks which were developing."
  • Electrolysis Tests on Treasure Island, 1939 June 5. MISC 1919 [3]#
    Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation" on electrical protection installed on Treasure Island's underground pipes. Describes the method of testing and the results.
  • Feather River power project : reports, photographs, maps, 1904-1906 M1884 [5]#
    Report, correspondence, photographs (94), and maps (27 with index), relating to a project undertaken for the Western Power Company of Los Angeles (later known as the Great Western Power Company) on the feasibility of creating a large reservoir at Big Meadows, on the North Fork of the Feather River (Plumas County, California), and creating a hydraulic power plant at Big Bend (on the North Fork) in order to deliver electric power to San Francisco and other places in northern California.
  • Felt Lake Dam photographs, 1929 PC0142 [5]#
    under a linear foot
    The materials consist of photographs documenting the construction of the Felt Lake Dam.
  • Joseph W. Gross research collection pertaining to water supply/control and flooding in California, 1890-1940 M1844 [5]#
    7 linear feet; 1909-1940
    An extensive collection pertaining to California water projects including printed research material, correspondence, official reports, maps, and over 2,600 captioned photographs He had a long career specializing as a "municipal and reclamation" engineer. This specialization had him working on all aspects of irrigation projects for specific water districts to consulting on flood control, especially relating to the Yuba, American, and Sacramento Rivers.
  • Mill creek flood control project : photograph collection, 1939-1942 MSS PHOTO 0285 [3]#
    44 cardboard sheets mounted with 138 black and white photographs. Images include personnel, work crews, equipment, aerial views, a few accidents, and site shots, some showing multiple shots of work progression at a specific location.
  • Report on a Coast Stream Water Supply for the Palo Alto Water District SCM0420 [5]#
    under a linear foot; 1930
    Preliminary report showing the feasibility of a coast stream water supply for the Palo Alto Water Disctrict.
  • Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection [7]#
    The Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection are materials owned and selected for digitization by the Santa Clara Valley Water District. The materials are related to water resources management in Santa Clara County, California dating in the early 1900s.
  • Santa Clara Valley water supply photographs, 1935-1938 MSS PHOTO 0627 [7]#
    under a linear foot
    The photographs depict the building of California dams.
  • Spring Valley Water Company records, 1905-1920 SCM0058 [4]#
    under a linear foot
    Legal papers documenting the agreements between the Spring Valley Water Company and Stanford University regarding Searsville Dam and Resevoir, 1919; and recordbook of measurements of the depth of Searsville Lake and amount of rainfall, 1905-1913, with some notes pertaining to pipes, water flow, and effect of the 1906 earthquake.
  • William W. Helbush collection of water project records MS 980 [7]#
    12 linear feet; 1905-1947
    William W. Helbush (circa 1895-1965) served as an engineer for the San Francisco Department of Public Works. The collection contains project records, including reports, contracts, notes, specifications, plans, blueprints, and site photographs, as well as administrative records, financial records, and reference material related to the design and construction of various water projects, most notably the Hetch Hetchy water supply project, the enlargement of O'Shaughnessy Dam, and the Richmond-Sunset sewage treatment plant and reservoir for the San Francisco Water Department.
No subdivision#1
  • Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996 M1414 [7]#
    10 linear feet
    Japanese American Toichi Domoto (1902-2001) was a noted horticulturist who began in his family's Domoto Brothers Nursery and later founded his own nursery in Hayward, California. The collection contains family and business correspondence, legal advice concerning the Alien Land Law of 1913, early nursery business records, early nursery catalogs (from the Yokohama nursery, the Domoto Bros. nursery, and Toichi Domoto's nursery), photographs of the Domoto family and early nursery business, class notes and subject files.

  • David L. Webster X-Ray slides PC0157 [8]#
    under a linear foot; 1888-1976
  • David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976 SC0131 [9]#
    35 linear feet
    He remained Professor of Physics at Stanford until 1954, when he retired. The papers of David Locke Webster document his career as a professor and physicist and include course material from physics classes taught at Stanford (1946-1954); notes and notebooks from his earlier teaching career at Harvard, Michigan and M.I.T.; correspondence and subject files on Army research projects; budget material for the Stanford physics department (1924-1943); reprints of articles; research data; photographs of apparatus used in experiments; manuscripts; correspondence (1939-70) regarding Webster's interests (e.g. Klystron Tube, compton effect); research notebooks (1916-1970); correspondence relating to the Physics Department during the 1940's; glass plates for printing graphs; photographs; maps.
Campus and student life#6
  • Bernice C. Rowell photographs PC0154 [3]#
    1900-1903
    Grandmother grew up in Fresno and attended Stanford in the 1900 to 1905 time frame. The first eighteen pictures provide a gallery of Stanford in the fall of 1900.
  • Florence Grace Savage photographs, circa 1904-1907 PC0068 [3]#

    Florence Mary Grace graduated from Stanford University in 1906 with an A.B. in math; while a student she was a member of the women's basketball team. Photographs of Stanford students and campus scenes including Memorial Church, quad views, campus entrance gates, Roble Hall, the Stanford Mausoleum, campus roads, reservoir on the former Peter Coutts estate, Encina Hall residents, football team, women's basketball team, student excursions off-campus, and Prof. Fernando Sanford.
  • Georgina Rolph scrapbook of her junior year, 1920-1921 M2154 [4]#

    Myron C. Burr earned his A.B. in civil engineering at Stanford University in May 1907. Subjects of the campus photographs include the Quad, Memorial Church, Encina dormitory rooms, club members on the porch of the Entre Nous eating club, athletics, and the laying of the last keystone in the outer Quad arcades.
  • Robert Jerome Snyder photographs, 1928 PC0099 [4]#
    under a linear foot
    Collection consists of two scrapbook pages of photographs and one illustration of football players, Coach Thornhill, and the construction of the Big Game bonfire, with one image of Herbert Hoover and family in front of the Hoover home on campus; and four images of the large hangar at Moffett Field, undated.
  • Student photograph album, 1889-circa 1930 (inclusive), 1905-1906 (bulk) A0088 [4]#

    Album, possibly kept by John Stephens Martin, with photographs of athletic players and games (football and baseball), dormitory rooms, and groups of male students, ca. 1905-1906; most of the athletic uniforms have a "B" or "Belmont" on them, probably representing the Belmont School in Belmnont, Calif. Engineering#6
  • Frank George Baum, "The Transformer" galleys SCM0116 [5]#

    Baum earned his engineering degree at Stanford University in 1898; he was assistant professor of electrical engineering at Stanford from 1898 to 1903. Galleys (incomplete) from his book, THE ALTERNATING CURRENT TRANSFORMER, with his corrections and annotations.
  • Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978 SC0160 [10]#

    The papers of Frederick Emmons Terman, dating from 1920 to 1978, document all phases of his long and influential career as an educator, electronics engineer, administrator, and author.   • Harris J. Ryan papers, 1908-1934 SC1034 [6]#

Ryan was a professor of electrical engineering at Stanford (1905-1931; emeritus, 1931-1934), head of the Department of Electrical Engineering and first director of the Ryan High Voltage Laboratory. Collection includes syllabi and notes on alternators, synchronous motors, transformers, transmission lines and other topics, 1899-1917; correspondence regarding a lecture tour of Japan, 1930-32; Harris' articles and publications, 1911-31; articles and clippings on the Ryan high voltage lab; guest book from the Ryan High Voltage Lab, 1920-1931; and biographical information and bibliographies.
  • Principles of Electrical Engineering : 32 weekly parts M1025 [3]#

    Experiments designed to illustrate fundamental points of electrical science.

  • Herbert Hoover letter to Frank A. Golder, 1924 SCM0033 [4*]#

    First located in Santa Clara, California. Chartered in 1851 as California Wesleyan College, soon changed to University of the Pacific.
Science and mathematics#17
  • Bailey Willis papers, circa 1900-1962 SC0200 [6]#
    1 linear foot
    He made geological research trips to China and Argentina, before coming to Stanford University in 1915 to succeed John C. Branner as head of the Department of Geology. Collection includes diagrams from Appalachian structures labeled "Experiments in Folding"; a pamphlet "Bailey Willis Speaks"; two typescript papers on geology, 1944 and undated; report on the San Andreas Fault Valley, ca. 1933; report of the Golden Gate Bridge & Highway District regarding Willis' criticism of the bridge foundation and his comment on the report, 1934-35; biographical materials, 1949-62; and a manuscript poem by Willis, 1939.
  • Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989 SC0474 [7]#

    French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Papers include correspondence, articles, speeches, manuscripts, lab notes, charts, and computer printouts pertaining largely to his research interests in the photosynthesis of purple bacteria, spectroscopy of plant pigments, and the construction of spectroscopic equipment.
  • Frank W. Weymouth papers, 1900-1965 SC0018 [3]#
    26 linear feet
    He rose through the various ranks to professorship in 1931 and becdame head of the Department of Physiology in 1938. Correspondence, research notes, poetry and prose manuscripts, lectures and research papers. Subjects include animal and human physiology and other related topics.
  • Geological map; San Juan Bautist Hills, 3 miles south of San Jose, California : hand-drawn and colored map, 1901, Jan.. MSS PRINTS 0167 4TH IN BOX [4]#

    under a linear foot

  • George Polya papers, 1884-1985 SC0337 [3]#
    75 linear feet; 1884-1987
    Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. Papers relate to Pólya's research and teaching in mathematics and include professional and personal correspondence with mathematicians worldwide, 1910-1984; course materials including lecture notes; mathematical research notebooks dating from 1917 to 1960; manuscripts including those from his published works Complex Variables , How to Solve It , Mathematical Discovery , and Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning ; ephemera; reprints; and photographs.
  • John Casper Branner papers, 1882-1921 SC0034 [8]#
    40 linear feet; 1882-1925
    The first professor to be named at the new Stanford University in 1891, Branner served as professor of geology at Stanford as well as executive head of the Geology Department. Personal papers of John Casper Branner including correspondence, manuscripts, field notebooks, photographs from field work, line drawings of geological formations, scrapbooks of photographs of the effects of the 1906 earthquake, report of the commission investigating the Panama Canal, slides, genealogies of the Baker and Branner families, and books and articles by Branner, many annotated.
  • John Casper Branner Photographs of San Francisco Earthquake, 1906 PC0206 [6]#
    under a linear foot; circa 1906
    The first professor to be named at the new Stanford University in 1891, Branner served as professor of geology at Stanford as well as executive head of the Geology Department. Photographic prints belonging to John Casper Branner documenting geological changes and property damage after the 1906 earthquake. Likely images from surveying group led by Branner, who was a member of the California State Earthquake Investigation Commission.
  • John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992 SC0745 [8]#
    8 linear feet
    He served as the first director of the Stanford Computation Center, 1953-61, taught the first programming course at Stanford in 1955, and helped found the computer science department at Stanford in 1965. These papers document his career as a mathematician and include his notes taken while a student at Brown University, 1937-41, and his master's and doctoral theses, 1940-41; research files (notes, computations, articles, computer printouts, some correspondence, and other materials) on Fourier series, Schlicht functions, spline theory, and other topics, 1940-83; memos, minutes, correspondence, and other records pertaining to Stanford's Dept. of Computer Sciences and the Stanford Computation Center, 1946-92; correspondence, notes, and reports pertaining to his Fulbright year, 1962-63; and bibliographic and biographical materials.
  • Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973 SC0298 [3]#

    Artificial collection of photographs chronicling the after-effects of the San Francisco Earthquake and Fire of 1906.   • Sidney Dean Townley papers, circa 1827-1939 SC0273 [6]#

  • William Russel Dudley papers, 1838-1937 (inclusive), 1864-1912 (bulk) SC0558 [5]#

  • Ephraim Douglass Adams papers, 1730-1974 (inclusive), 1900-1931 (bulk) SC0142 [4*]#

Personal and professional correspondence, drafts, manuscripts and research notes for various publications, and other papers.

Rowell, Benjamin Ide Wheeler, and Ray Lyman Wilbur. Also includes diaries, notes, photographs, newsclippings, pamphlets, published works, medals, and memorabilia.

  • David Starr Jordan Papers [7]#
    Jordan was a naturalist-first a botanist and secondly and of greater significance an ichthyologist. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's voluminous correspondence (62.25 linear ft.) relating to professional and university matters, but also contains other types of material such as writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. He developed the idea of a junior college and was responsible for developing Stanford University into an intellectually competitive university rather than the technical training school envisioned by the founders.
  • David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981 SC0058 [8]#
    266 linear feet
    In the Spring of 1891, Leland Stanford offered Jordan the presidency of the university established in memory of the late son of Leland Stanford and Jane Lathrop Stanford. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's correspondence relating to professional and university matters, and also contains writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. Materials in the collection reflect Jordan's embrace of and advocacy for eugenics, including his leadership in 19th and 20th century eugenics organizations.

Franklin, 1923-32; fundraising letter from Herbert Hoover re the Stanford Re-investment Fund ca. 1940; letter and menu for Sigma Xi President's Dinner, 1924; booklet on Palo Alto, ca. 1930; and photographs of a Stanford chemistry lab and the cactus garden on campus.

  • George E. Crothers papers, 1905-1957 SC0130 [8]#

    under a linear foot
    Allene Thorpe Lamson, wife of Stanford Press employee David Lamson, was found dead in her campus home on Memorial Day 1933. David Lamson was charged with her murder, tried and convicted, but was granted a new trial; all charges against him were dropped in April 1936. Collection includes clippings about the murder of Allene Thorpe Lamson and the trials of David Lamson, 1933-1992; photocopy of the testimony of police chief H. A. Zink; original typescript of D. L. Webster's "Notes on Investigation of the Physical Evidence in the Lamson Bathroom," with accompanying photographs, 1934; three notebooks kept during the trials, partially using shorthand (no author noted); copy of Russell and Winters' book THE CASE OF DAVID LAMSON (1934); photographs of the house the Lamsons lived in, taken in 1992; and miscellaneous materials on David and Allene Lamson copied from various Stanford publications.

One of several of sharing the name, this collection contains multiple accessions from various donors over many years, including a ledger from an English sailing vessel dated 1711-1757, railroad stock and bond certificates signed by Hopkins and Huntington, deeds and legal documents involving a variety of rail companies (including the signatures of founding stockholders for the Oakland Railroad Co. in 1868), and a great deal of Southern Pacific Railroad material, some of which was sent directly to the Hopkins Library while it was under the care of director Jeanette Hitchcock in the 1940s.
  • Hopkins transportation collection, 1844-1969 (inclusive), 1936-1954 (bulk) M0200 [4]#
    18 linear feet
    Ephemera related to the construction and operation of railroads in the Western United States and the United Kingdom, including dispatcher's records from Beaumont, California; Los Angeles, California; and Mexicali, Baja California. While primarily about railroads, the collection also contains printed material and ephemera about other forms of transport, including automobiles, passenger ships, and airplanes, as well as various mostly related engineering plans and reports.
  • Newsclipping collection, 1890-1952 M1236 [3]#
    1 linear foot
    A miscellaneous collection, including railroad history, ca. 1940-1952, ramifications of the Clayton Act which outlawed as monopolistic the agreements railroads had formed among themselves, aviation in the post World War II era and a bit about its advent, many articles on the effect of World War II on railroads, municipal railroads, particularly in San Francisco, ships for trade and leisure, and a few clippings about the Hopkins family and the sale of the Hopkins house to Hollywood in the 1940s.
  • Railroads and trolleys in the United States and Mexico : photographs MSS.PHOTO.0201 [6]#
    2 linear feet; 1889-1972
    Collection contains over 2,600 photographs documenting various railways and trolley lines in the United States (primarily California) and Mexico.
  • Railway and locomotive historical societies : album, 1940-1958 M1157 [5]#
    1 linear foot
    During the 1950s there were several important local organizations devoted to railroad history: The Pacific Coast Railroad and Locomotive Historical Society, Inc., the California-Nevada Railroad Historical Society, the Bay Area Electric Railroad Association, and the Central Railway Club of San Jose. Society newsletters and magazines, rail excursion flyers, excursion photographs, news clippings, announcements, time tables, ticket stubs, map, etc.
  • San Francisco International Airport : album, 1954-1955 MSS CODEX 0027 FF [4]#
    Album prepared as a promotional piece for the British Overseas Airways Corporation and for Lufthansa on the opening of San Francisco International Airport. Ephemera includes photographs; plot and elevation plans; booklet on statistical facts of air traffic; brochures and data describing San Francisco and the airport.
  • William Ripley Dorr collection of California railroad club photograph albums MSS.PHOTO.0416 [3]#
    1948-1960
    William Ripley Dorr, a resident of Palos Verdes Estates, California, was a confirmed rail fan. Dorr photographed each trip, and mounted the photographs in two albums, which comprise the collection. They are mainly examples of types of engines and types of cars, from both the era of steam and the more modern diesel era.
Water and public works#1
  • Electrolysis tests on Treasure Island, 1940, 1940 December 19. MISC 1920 [4]#
    Report on wear and tear of Treasure Island's infrastructure, especially water leakage and salt-water intrusion, "Requested by P.M. Downing and L.J. Brown, Construction Superintendent, Golden Gate International Exposition." Includes six original tipped-in photographs and nine folding plans of various portions of Treasure Island, showing the location of water-system tests in relation to specific proposed exhibition space, etc.
No subdivision#3
  • Albert Wilson papers, ca. 1910-1995 M1397 [5]#
    32 linear feet
    Albert Wilson (1903-1996), was a San Francisco Bay Area botanist, landscape architect, author, teacher and lecturer on gardening and landscaping, as well as a TV and radio talk show personality who wrote several books popularizing gardening, as well as an autobiography. Material related to Wilson's career as horticulturalist, author, and broadcaster.
  • California Flower Market records, 1890-2014 MS 4142 [8]#
    11 linear feet
    The California Flower Market, Inc. was founded in 1912 by Japanese American flower growers in the San Francisco Bay Area. The records of the California Flower Market, Inc. include photographs, photograph albums, manuscript materials, books, articles, ephemera, and audiovisual materials from the late 1800s to 2014, with the bulk covering the period 1910 to 1990.
  • Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996 M1414 [7]#
    10 linear feet
    Japanese American Toichi Domoto (1902-2001) was a noted horticulturist who began in his family's Domoto Brothers Nursery and later founded his own nursery in Hayward, California. The collection contains family and business correspondence, legal advice concerning the Alien Land Law of 1913, early nursery business records, early nursery catalogs (from the Yokohama nursery, the Domoto Bros. nursery, and Toichi Domoto's nursery), photographs of the Domoto family and early nursery business, class notes and subject files.
Education and research#150
Applied physics#12
  • Albert V. Baez papers, 1949-1995 SC1052 [7]#
    21 linear feet
    The materials consist of research files, correspondence, teaching materials, biographical material, publications, photographs, and some experimental equipment. Albert Vinicio Baez, Ph.D. (1912-2007) was a prominent Mexican-American physicist, and the father of singers Joan Baez and Mimi Fariña. In 1948, along with Stanford University professor Paul Kirkpatrick (1894–1992), Baez developed the X-ray reflection microscope for examination of living cells.
  • Anthony Edward Siegman papers, 1916-2013 (inclusive) SC1171 [8]#
    54 linear feet; 1916-2014
    Anthony Siegman was an electrical engineer, primarily focused on masers and lasers. Siegman became an assistant professor at Stanford in Electrical Engineering in 1957. The materials consist of administrative files, research files, correspondence, and publications.
  • Bloch symposium; a Stanford centennial symposium celebrating the work of Felix Bloch [videorecording] V0052 [6]#
    1 linear foot; 1989
    Excelling in both theoretical and experimental physics, Bloch won the Nobel Prize in 1952 for his work in nuclear magnetism. Tapes from a symposium held on October 27 and 28, 1989, at Stanford University; speakers included Robert Hofstadter, James S. Harris, William A. Little, K. Halbach, Erwin Hahn, D. Fisher, H. Gutfreund, Alexander Pines, E. Raymond Andrew, and W.F. Brinkman.
    [About half of this symposium, on Felix Bloch's work in nuclear magnetism that won the Nobel Prize in 1952, concerns this period.]
  • C. F. Quate papers, circa 1961-1984 SC0347 [8]#
    14 linear feet
    He joined the Stanford faculty in 1961 as professor in the applied physics and electrical engineering departments, serving two terms as chair of the department of applied physics. Correspondence, memoranda, press releases, contracts, grants, course materials and other records pertaining to his research and teaching at Stanford, including work at the Ginzton Laboratory; and offsets, glossies, and slides from the acoustic microscope project.
  • David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976 SC0131 [9]#
    35 linear feet
    He remained Professor of Physics at Stanford until 1954, when he retired. The papers of David Locke Webster document his career as a professor and physicist and include course material from physics classes taught at Stanford (1946-1954); notes and notebooks from his earlier teaching career at Harvard, Michigan and M.I.T.; correspondence and subject files on Army research projects; budget material for the Stanford physics department (1924-1943); reprints of articles; research data; photographs of apparatus used in experiments; manuscripts; correspondence (1939-70) regarding Webster's interests (e.g. Klystron Tube, compton effect); research notebooks (1916-1970); correspondence relating to the Physics Department during the 1940's; glass plates for printing graphs; photographs; maps.
  • Felix Bloch papers, 1928-1987 SC0303 [9]#
    36 linear feet; 1931-1987
    The Bloch papers document Felix Bloch's role in twentieth century physics as a scientist, teacher and administrator. The collection includes correspondence, grant proposals, lecture notes, minutes and accompanying documentation regarding departmental, university and national committees, research notebooks, grants, patents, and designs; files regarding organizations in which Bloch played an active role; publications (predominantly reprints) by Bloch; and photographs.
  • Fu Chun Yu lab notebooks [facsimiles], 1949-1950 SC0995 [7]#
    under a linear foot
    Collection consists of three notebooks (in facsimile) kept by Fu Chun Yu while he was a post-doc in Prof. Felix Bloch's NMR laboratory at Stanford; they cover Yu's work with Warren Proctor that lead to a realization of the chemical shift in molecules.
  • High Frequency Direct Writing Oscillograph Project Lantern Slides, circa 1960s PC0212 [7]#
    1 linear foot
    Richard G. Sweet developed an ink-jet recorder at Stanford University in the early 1960s. Funded by an Army Signal Corps contract, Sweet developed a technique for selective charging and deflection of individual ink droplets, resulting in higher recording speeds for ink-jet printers.
  • Nuclear resonance : glass slides, ca. 1945 M1061 [3]#
    1940
    Slides show measuring equipment and graphs and measurements.
  • Optics and laser spectroscopy, Bell Telephone Laboratories, 1951-1961, and Stanford University since 1961 : oral history transcript / 1998 OH-066 [7]#
    co-author, with Charles H. Townes, of Microwave Spectroscopy (1955), dealing with theory and experimental techniques of microwave spectroscopy; marriage in 1951 to Aurelia Townes, and move to Bell Telephone Laboratories: working on superconductivity, in 1957-1958 collaborating with Townes on the optical maser (laser), and publication of "Infrared and Optical Masers"; discussion of the atmosphere at Columbia and at Bell Labs, pressures, publications, patents; joins physics faculty at Stanford University: research group in laser spectroscopy, Ted Hänsch, students, administrative matters, other faculty.
  • Paul Harmon Kirkpatrick autobiography, 1971 SCM0086 [5]#
    under a linear foot
    Professor of physics at Stanford University since 1931 (emeritus, 1960 - ); best known for his pioneering work in x-ray technology. General reminiscences about his life, including recollections about his work and colleagues at Stanford.
    [About half of this autobiography, recollections of his work and colleagues at Stanford before his retirement in 1960, concerns this period.]
  • Stanford University, W.W. Hansen Laboratories of Physics, records, 1947-1993 SC0062 [9]#
    37 linear feet
    Contracts, proposals, correspondence, and memoranda from the files of the William W. Hansen Laboratories relating to the construction of the Stanford Linear Accelerator, the development of the Klystron tube, and medical research using linear accelerators.

  • Chicanismo 7750/4 MECHA BOX 1 [4]#

    Official publication for MEChA, Stanford University.

    Mary Hill Skougaard (AB 1950 in communications) was the first female station manager at Stanford?s student radio station, KZSU. Copy negatives of original images in a scrapbook owned by Mary Hill Skougaard, with photocopies of most of the original images. Subjects include KZSU engineers and staff, live broadcasts, and parties; individuals include Bill Kane, Fred Steiner, Rosemarie Armstrong [Ostberg], Peter F. Dawson, Mary Hill [Skougaard], and Steve Phillips.
  • Stanford Amateur Radio Club scrapbook, 1941-1957 SC0885 [4]#
    under a linear foot
    The "ham radio" station W6YX at Stanford dates back to 1924 and is still active; electronics professor Oswald G. Villard Jr. served as faculty advisor and trustee for many years. Scrapbook contains clippings, articles, correspondence, membership list, certificates (one issued to Osward G. Villard), photographs, and 1 FCC complaint; some of the correspondence is with the American Radio Relay League regarding records of calls made by the club.
  • Stanford Villager's Cook Book SCM0435 [3]#

    The Stanford Village complex was developed from converted military housing located in Menlo Park on the current site of SRI International. Cookbook compiled by Stanford Village residents, 1961. Recipes include Meats, Casseroles; Salads, Vegetables; Breads; Cakes, Cookies, Pies, Desserts.
Education research and educational technology#3
  • Patrick Suppes papers, 1951-2014 SC1241 [8]#
    154 linear feet
    Patrick Suppes was the Lucie Stern Professor of Philosophy, Emeritus, and a member of the departments of Statistics and Psychology and of the Graduate School of Education at Stanford University. This collection consists of research, notes, papers, and correspondence with a particular emphasis on Suppes' work on computer-assisted education research.
  • Pauline Snedden Sears papers, 1931-1990 (inclusive), 1953-1977 (bulk) SC0501 [3]#
    2 linear feet
    Before joining the Stanford faculty in the School of Education in 1953, she taught at Yale and Harvard and was a research associate at the Child Welfare Research Station at the State University of Iowa. Her research subjects included the classroom effects of computer assisted instruction, development of creativity, and teaching strategies for effective reinforcement of culturally different children. The papers of Pauline Sears primarily pertain to her career at Stanford, with only one folder of materials pertaining to her activities during the 1930s.
  • Stanford Consultation Services records, 1949-1956 SC0481 [4]#
    9 linear feet
    The Stanford Consultation Services, under the direction of Education Professor Robert N. Bush, conducted case studies of teachers and administrators in selected school systems in California, Colorado, Washington, and Australia. Records include complete case files from three individual studies at Alameda High School in Alameda, CA, MR Trace Elementary School in San Jose, CA, and Jordan Junior High School in Palo Alto, CA; summary folders from all other cases; and general administrative files.
Engineering#11
  • Bernard Roth papers SC1602 [8*]#
    2 linear feet; undated
    Bernard Roth, Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Emeritus, is one of the founders of the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford (the d.school) and is active in its development: currently, he serves as Academic Director.
  • Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978 SC0160 [10]#
    158 linear feet
    The papers of Frederick Emmons Terman, dating from 1920 to 1978, document all phases of his long and influential career as an educator, electronics engineer, administrator, and author. The collection consists of nearly 200 boxes of correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, speeches and miscellaneous materials accumulated by Dr. Terman and his staff throughout his professional life.
  • Glen E. Myers Stanford class notes, 1956-1962 SC0675 [3]#
    3 linear feet
    Glen E. Myers studied mechanical engineering at Stanford, earning his M.S. in 1957 and his Ph.D. in 1962. This collection contains syllabi, course handouts, problem sets, exams, and Myers' notes from engineering, math, and physics classes he took at Stanford, 1956-59; for the elementary engineering thermodynamics classes for which he was a teaching assistant, 1958-59; and for the class on elementary engineering thermodynamics that he taught at Stanford during the summer of 1962.
  • H.O. Fuchs papers, 1950-1988 SC0101 [4]#
    32 linear feet
    Course notes for mechanical engineering undergraduate and graduate classes; correspondence; case histories in engineering problems prepared by Fuchs; records pertaining to the Engineering Case Program; research notes, articles, and papers by Fuchs; and photographs. Fuchs, an expert on fatique in metals, taught mechanical engineering at Stanford University from 1964 to 1973, when he became an Emeritus Professor.
  • John Edward Arnold course materials, 1958-1959 SCM0046 [8]#
    under a linear foot; 1958-2016
    John Edward Arnold was a professor of mechanical engineering and business administration at Stanford University. He was the founding director of the Design Division of the Mechanical Engineering Department. Lectures on creativity from the Creative Engineering Seminar, 1959, by Arnold and guest lecturers J.P. Guilford, Robert S. Hartman, and Robert H. McKim; a lecture by A. H. Maslow, "Emotional Blocks to Creativity," presented to U.S. Army engineers at Fort Belvoir, VA, 1958; a chart on creative process; and a bibliography on creative engineering.
  • John Edward Arnold Papers [8]#
    Lectures on creativity from the Creative Engineering Seminar, 1959, by Arnold and guest lecturers J.P. Guilford, Robert S. Hartman, and Robert H. McKim; a lecture by A. H. Maslow, "Emotional Blocks to Creativity, " presented to U.S. Army engineers at Fort Belvoir, VA, 1958; a chart on creative process; and a bibliography on creative engineering.
  • Neal Van Devender papers, 1964-2003 (inclusive), 1964-1966 (bulk) SC0893 [3]#
    2 linear feet
    Neal Van Devender earned his master's degree in aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University in 1966. The bulk of the collection consists of syllabi, notes, homework reports, and exams from math, engineering and aeronautics classes at Stanford, 1965-66.
  • Stanford University, Engineering Case Program, case files, 1948-1972 SC0269 [6]#
    4 linear feet
    The Engineering Case Program, which began at Stanford University in 1964, provided written accounts of engineering problems to be used in the training of engineers. This collection consists of the master files from 114 cases where the author was a Stanford faculty or staff member or the event described happened in the San Francisco Bay Area.
  • Stanford University, Foundry, records, 1945-1952 (inclusive) SC1121 [4]#
    under a linear foot
    The Stanford Foundry operated by mechanical engineering students in the mid-20th century. The materials consist of news clippings, photographs, and negatives documenting the Stanford University Foundry.
  • Stephen Timoshenko papers, 1907-1996 (inclusive), 1921-1970 (bulk) SC0641 [7]#
    10 linear feet
    Stephen Prokofievitch Timoshenko, a world-renowned authority on theoretical and applied mechanics, was educated at the Munich Polytechnic Institute and at the University of Gottingen. Correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, galleys, notes, reprints, photographs, passports, awards, and other items; some materials are in Russian or German.
  • Wilhelm Flügge papers, 1937-1980 SC0384 [6]#
    10 linear feet
    Wilhelm Flügge, internationally known specialist in engineering mechanics, is best known for his research on shell structures. These papers, dating from 1937-1980, pertain primarily to his professional career at Stanford; included are correspondence, manuscripts, papers, lectures, minutes, memoranda, photographs, and teaching materials.

  • ARS Audiotape Collection ARS.0070 [3]#

  • Arthur Kornberg papers, 1938-2007 SC0359 [9]#

  • Benjamin M. Page papers, 1929-1996 SC0414 [4]#
    53 linear feet
    Geologist. Page's special fields are structural geology and the relationship between geological structures and plate tectonics. Papers include correspondence, minutes, budgets, class notes, course files, student papers, reports, maps, and research files and pertain to his activities as professor, department administrator, and scientist.
  • C.B. Niel papers, 1923-1977 SC0325 [3]#

The STOP AIDS Project records are comprised of behavioral risk assessment surveys; social marketing campaign materials, including HIV/AIDS prevention posters and flyers; community outreach and workshop materials; volunteer training materials; correspondence; grant proposals; fund development materials; administrative records; photographs; audio and video recordings; and computer files.
  • William C. Dement papers, circa 1960s-1990s SC0633 [3]#
    208 linear feet
    William C. Dement is Professor Emeritus in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford. He founded the Sleep Research Center at Stanford and co-founded the Sleep Research Society. Collection mainly consists of correspondence, administrative records from various sleep research organizations he was involved in, and sleep studies and research.

  • Gschwind / Swent, Langan, Waterman, Mendenhall, and Herz Family papers M1979 [5]#

Philanthropy and foundations#5
  • Anne Firth Murray papers, 1970-2018 SC1412 [3]#
    40 linear feet; circa 1970s-2018
    For the past twenty-five years, she has worked in the field of philanthropy, serving as a consultant to many foundations. She is the Founding President of The Global Fund for Women, which provides funds internationally to seed, strengthen, and link groups committed to women's well being. Papers include Murray's Global Fund for Women and Hewlett Foundation files; teaching files; professional files; and subject files.
  • David and Lucile Packard: A lifetime of Stanford philanthropy SCM0430 [3]#
    under a linear foot; 2013
    Dave and Lucile Packard's philanthropic activities have had a major impact on Stanford University through grants provided through the the David and Lucile Packard Foundation.
  • Global Fund for Women records, 1964-2014 SC0671 [5]#
    38 linear feet
    The Global Fund for Women was founded in Palo Alto, Calif. in 1987 by Anne Firth Murray, Frances Kissling and Laura Lederer. Its mission is to support women's rights by providing grant funds to women's organizations throughout the world. The records consist of files from Anne Firth Murray's tenure as Founding President of the Global Fund for Women (1987-1996). Included are chronological files from Firth and other administrators, correspondence, clippings and articles, press releases and other promotional materials, and meeting and event files.
  • William Hewlett Memorial Service [videorecording] V0212 [8*]#
    under a linear foot; 2001
    Service was held in Stanford University's Memorial Church on January 20, 2001; includes tributes by Herant Katchadourian, Maggie Lacey Schneider, Arjay Miller, David W. Packard, and Walter B. Hewlett. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
  • William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001) M1995 [10]#
    316 linear feet
    William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. Following the tremendous success of Hewlett-Packard, he became well known for his philanthropy, donating millions of dollars from his fortune to support various causes. The William Hewlett papers consists of correspondence, photographs, financial records, reports, minutes, calendars, hardware, electronic files, videotapes, newspaper clippings, publications, and other materials.

    Him Mark Lai was a writer, historian, and archivist of Chinese America. This collection primarily consists of his own family history, particularly that of the Mark/Mai clan, and his parents' immigration to California.
  • Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area : ephemera from Eve Sutton, 1980-2004 M1280 [6]#
    3 linear feet
    Primarily material from Palo Alto and Stanford University, including Congregation Kol Emeth, Stanford Hillel, Resource magazine, and the Bureau of Jewish Education.
  • Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1981-2010 M0939 [4]#
    12 linear feet; 1981-2008
    The collection documents non-traditional Jewish life in the Bay Area, especially newsletters and announcements from various organizations. There are also liturgical creations around life-cycle events. Material collected by Roger S. Kohn and Zachary M. Baker, both Stanford University Library curators, from local synagogues, individuals, organizations, and businesses.
  • Ken and Caretha Coleman archive of Black histories in Silicon Valley, circa 2020s M2612 [8]#
    Collection includes oral histories of Harry Bremond, Caretha Coleman, Al Cotton, Kathy Cotton, Peggy Forbes, Maynard Holliday, Pamela Isom, Max Pearl, Marc Ramsey. Additional material related to African Americans in Silicon Valley forthcoming.
  • No Boundaries - The Digital Nomads of Estonia, 1947-1953 SC1386 [7]#
    2016-2017
    Oral history interviews with Estonians whose lives have been changed by the intersection of the country's digital revolution and its rejoining of the free world; ranging from key people involved with initiating and shaping the policies that made the digital revolution possible, to those who grew up with, and were able to make full use of, the new possibilities to learn, create and live in the new, interconnected world, focusing on Estonians who have migrated to California's Silicon Valley.
  • Shau Wing Chan papers, 1911-1994 SC0421 [3]#
    7 linear feet
    He joined the Stanford faculty in 1938 and retired in 1972. He was instrumental in founding what is now the Department of Asian Languages, serving as its executive head from 1958-1962. Notebooks, exams, reading notes, and a draft of his thesis from his graduate studies, 1930-1933; professional and personal correspondence, 1938-1949, including letters pertaining to his immigration status; correspondence, memoranda, and reports pertaining to Stanford administrative and departmental matters, 1935-1982; and family papers, 1911-1994.
  • The Baltic video archive : Baltic video testimonies at Stanford Libraries [5]#
    2018
    The Baltic Video Archive of Stanford Libraries consists of four oral history collections, each of which tells the story of the Baltic countries through video testimonies of the Baltic peoples. The archive also includes stories told by the more recent generation, the so-called “digital nomads,” or the “Estonian mafia,” who have migrated to and established enterprises in California's Silicon Valley.

Women, gender and sexuality#4
  • Elizabeth Lyman papers, 1958-2009 (inclusive) SC0224 [8]#
    187 linear feet
    Elizabeth "Jing" Lyman (1925-2013) was communitiy activist who organized and sustained many foundations and coalitions, including Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and the Women's Resource Center, among many others. Primarily files relating to Jing Lyman's activities in community affairs, the Women's Resource Center, the Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and with various foundations and executive boards. Jing Lyman played an instrumental role in creating what is now the Michelle R. Clayman Institute for Gender Research at Stanford.
  • Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Awareness Program records, 1988-2000 (inclusive), 1997-2000 (bulk) SC0945 [5]#
    4 linear feet
    The Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Awareness Program, formed in 1985, worked to end intolerance and stereotypes of lesbian, gay and bisexual persons. Collection consists largely of the evaluation forms completed by students at Bay Area high schools and colleges following a presentation; other records include training manuals, speakers' resources, and clippings.
  • Oral histories of young lesbian, bisexual, transgender and intersexed Jewish women of the San Francisco Bay Area, 1996 M0959 [3]#
    1 linear foot
  • YWCA of the Mid-Peninsula records, circa 1948-2013 M1538 [9]#
    51 linear feet
    The YWCA of the Mid-Peninsula opened in 1948 as a recreation center for business women. It expanded to provide recreational and social services for women that met the organization's mission of "empowering women and eliminating racism." This collection documents the organization's history, its administrative structure and daily operations, major programming and public policy efforts, and ties to the Stanford and national YWCA.

Armed forces and military history#1
  • The Battle of 73 Easting, Gulf War : simulation project papers, 1991-1993 M1451 [7]#
    5 linear feet
    Papers concerning the simulation of a tank battle in the 1991 Gulf War. Arms control, science and technology policy#4
  • "Cyberspace" [videorecording] V0243 [5]#
    under a linear foot; 2002
    Tapes of the program held in Kresge Auditorium on Sept. 18, 2002, on the national cybersecurity draft plan [The National Strategy to Secure Cyberspace]; speakers included Robert Mueller, Richard Clarke, Jennifer Granick, and Cedric Bennett.
  • Computers, Freedom, and Privacy conference papers, Judi Clark collection, 1991-1997 M1040 [8]#
    5 linear feet
    Judi Clark was one of the organizers of the annual conference of Computers, Freedom, and Privacy (CFP), which started in 1991. Conference presentation topics included freedom of speech protections, security of personal data stored by private companies, government regulation and technology, and cultivating civility on Internet bulletin boards. The collection includes published conference proceedings in print, audio, and video formats for the first three conferences held during the 1990s; and supplemental conference materials including position papers submitted by speakers and presentations given by companies on developing strategies for an Internet presence.
  • John Young papers and Cryptome archive, circa 1980-2025 M3168 [7]#
  • Michael M. May papers SC1060 [5]#
    18 linear feet; 1970-2009
    Michael May is Professor Emeritus (Research) in the Stanford University School of Engineering and a senior fellow with the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies at Stanford University. The primary topics include May's work for CISAC (Committee on International Security and Arms Control) - which includes research on nuclear proliferation, management of plutonium, and international relations - as well as logistical planning to do with May's travels, conferences, and papers.

    The papers of Richard A. Stepp pertain largely to the time he spent in Burma as an advisor on technical services for small industries, 1958-59. Included are correspondence, notebooks, reports, memos, Burmese government documents (in English), other publications, and photographs, 1954-59.
  • Robert Slobodan Djurdjevic papers, 1978-1997 90077 BOX 1 [4]#

    This collection documents the Blue Ribbon Commission on Improving Custody Operations, Santa Clara County, 2015.   • Fred Turner papers, 1968-2019 SC1146 [8]#
    12 linear feet
    Fred Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication at Stanford University and Director of Stanford's Program in Science, Technology, and Society. Files consist primarily of research material, manuscripts, and chapter drafts related to Turner's book, From Counterculture to Cyberculture: Stewart Brand, the Whole Earth Network, and the Rise of Digital Utopianism.

    Howard Rheingold (b.1947) is an author, teacher, and critic whose focus is primarily on technology and communication media. He was editor of Whole Earth Review and the Millennium Whole Earth Catalog (1994). The papers of writer and technologist Howard Rheingold include drafts, proposals, and other typescripts; notes; fliers; and many articles and videos by and about him.   • New Dimensions Media records, 1968-2024 M1577 [8*]#
    640 linear feet; 1968-2016
    The New Dimensions Foundation is an independent, listener supported, educational broadcasting group based in Ukiah, California. New Dimensions might be superficially described as about new age philosophy and self-help; as their website says, "Our purpose is to share knowledge that has the potential to deepen our connections to self, family, community, planet and the natural world. We encourage public awareness of various approaches towards creating a world that works for everyone." Recordings and files from long-running radio program New Dimensions Radio, along with recordings of related programming.
  • Stewart Brand papers, 1954-2000 M1237 [10]#
    53 linear feet
    He was loosely associated with the Merry Pranksters, USCO, and other countercultural groups, and spent much of the 1960s traveling and visiting communal experiments. Brand created the original Whole Earth Catalog in 1968 to provide practical information on tools that would be useful for people creating and living in communes. The Steward Brand papers contains correspondence, personal journals, manuscripts, photographs, project records, articles, and publications.

  • Bucky Conversations: Conversations on the Life and Work of an Enigmatic Genius, 2002-2003 M1915 [8*]#
    7 linear feet; 2002-2004
    In 2002, to celebrate the acquisition of the Fuller archive, the Stanford University Libraries and the Stanford Humanities Laboratory launched a series of Conversations on R. Buckminster Fuller, alias "Bucky," inventor of the Dymaxion car, the Dymaxion Dwelling Unit, and the geodesic dome, author of Utopia or Oblivion, 4D Timelock, Synergetics, Tetrascroll and Critical Path. The series consists of filmed interviews with Fuller's key collaborators, interlocutors and contemporaries, and is designed to enhance critical understanding of Fuller and his work.
